newsitem.title: USA: Goldman expects Fed tightening over coming year.
newsitem.headline: Goldman expects Fed tightening over coming year.

text.p: Goldman, Sachs & Co forecasts that the Federal Reserve will tighten monetary policy by about 125 basis points over the next year and a half, said William Dudley, the firm's director of U.S. economic research.

"In terms of our forecast, what we are looking for is about 125 basis points in tightening over the next year to year and a half," said Dudley at a foreign exchange conference here sponsored by Goldman.

Dudley said the timing of a credit tightening by the Federal Reserve is uncertain. "But I'd say if the data continues like they have so far this week, for the remainder of the week, that we are not talking about a tightening until the first quarter of next year."

Dudley explained that the reason for Goldman's predictions are based on its expectation of a rebound in consumer spending. In addition, the firm also does not assess the current monetary policy regime as tight, he said.
Goldman expects a tightening to precipitate a selloff in bonds with yields backing up to about 7-to-7-1/2 pct, he said.
